messages:
Aisha (CS): FYI getting a report from Sam's team — their browser integration started seeing intermittent 503s during onboarding. They said failures spike when a user opens a page with several widgets at once. 
Sam (Customer): yep — reproducible for us. open 3 product pages -> each fires 5 parallel embed calls -> ~20% of requests get 503s for a few seconds. Happens on Chrome only. No auth errors, just 503s.
Aisha (CS): thanks. Sam can you paste the snippet you use in the page?
Sam (Customer): sure — it's basically the quickstart with a naive init per widget: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ key: 'pk_live_XXX' });
widgets.forEach(w => client.embed(w.payload));
```
Sam (Customer): we create a new client per widget (oops), so lots of parallel connections.
dev_jordan: that pattern will fan out tokens from the browser and spike our edge. 503 is our edge returning overloaded backend. Can you try reusing a single client instance and throttle concurrency?
Sam (Customer): ok will try, any recommended params?
ryan-eng-runtime: start with a single shared client and set a client-side cap like PromisePool size 4. If you're using our browser SDK you can do: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ key: 'pk_live_XXX', maxConcurrentRequests: 4 });
```
(If your SDK version doesn't expose that param, we have a helper util in our docs.)
marta (solutions): also, browser tokens should be short-lived and proxied when possible. If you must call directly from the client, reuse the same token instance so it doesn't open separate upstream sessions. For immediate relief we can enable a temporary soft-limit increase on the account while you migrate to a pooled client. Ping if you want that. :white_check_mark:
oliver (eng-ml): another lever — if your workload is many small embedding calls, consider batching on the client or using the chunking helper to combine N items per request. That will reduce per-request overhead and KV cache churn.
Sam (Customer): batching sounds good. Any example?
oliver (eng-ml): quick example: 
```js
const batch = chunk(items, 8);
for (const b of batch) await client.embed({ inputs: b });
```
This drops requests by ~8x.
dev_jordan: we'll also check the edge logs for Sam's org id — if we see hot bursts we can add a short retry-after header and a non-throttling queue for onboarding accounts. Sam, can you share the org id and a 5-min window when it happened?
Sam (Customer): org_9x7. Last happened 2026-03-20 15:12-15:18 UTC. I sent HAR and console logs to Aisha DM.
deploy-bot: Deploy finished: edge-rate-cap-tuner v2.14 → prod (by ryan-eng-runtime) :rocket:
ryan-eng-runtime: we pushed a small edge tuning last hour that should reduce transient 503s for small bursts, but it won't fix a constant fanout. If you still see errors after switching to a shared client + batching, we'll fast-path a trial on Dedicated for onboarding traffic.
Aisha (CS): Action items: 1) Sam to switch to shared client + cap concurrency and report results by EOD PT; 2) Oliver to send a short batching snippet to Sam; 3) Ryan to peek edge logs for org_9x7 and let us know if we applied a temporary soft-limit bump. I'll follow up and book a 30-min troubleshooting call if needed.
Sam (Customer): thanks all — implementing pooled client now, will update in ~2hrs. :pray:
Aisha (CS): great — appreciate it. If this looks like a renewal risk we'll prioritize a Dedicated trial while they complete integration.
ryan-eng-runtime: noted. I'll post logs in this thread when I have them.
Aisha (CS): marking as tracking: onboarding->integration flakiness. Keeping thread open.
